app.title: Cascade reservoir scheduling API (Swagger UI)
app.summary: A person downloads the bundled sample input workbook or prepares their own, then uploads it to the compute endpoint and picks a daily, ten-day or monthly time step and an output format. The service splits the workbook into per-reservoir inputs and simulates an upper and a lower reservoir in series, step by step: water balance, releases, supply to users, top-up from the upper reservoir, and hydropower output. It sums the per-step results by month, calendar year and hydrological year. The person gets back a results workbook, or JSON with a preview of the input parameters, the result tables, chart-ready series of water level, flow and power, and the workbook encoded in base64.

task.text: Simulate how two reservoirs in series operate over a historical inflow record, then summarise their water levels, supply, shortages and power output by period.

data.text: A multi-sheet input workbook with run parameters and, for each reservoir, characteristics (dead, flood-limit and normal water levels), level–storage and level–discharge curves, inflow and demand series, limit lines and operating rules. Output is per-step and aggregated time series tables for each reservoir.
data.item: one reservoir's state over one time step (a day, a ten-day period or a month)

stage.text: running operating simulations on prepared inflow and reservoir parameters, before reporting the scheduling results

mechanism.text: The interface is the auto-generated Swagger page over a small HTTP API. A sample endpoint serves an input workbook, and a compute form takes the uploaded workbook, a time step and an output format. Compute returns either a results workbook to download or JSON with an input preview, result tables, and date-keyed series for level, flow and power charts.

field.text: cascade reservoir operation and hydropower scheduling in water resources engineering

workflow.name: run a simulation model from a parameter workbook and export the results

steps.here: GET /api/sample downloads the bundled input workbook as a template. The person then uploads their own workbook to the compute form's file field.
The calc_step field takes 日 / 旬 / 月 (daily, ten-day or monthly) and anything else is rejected. The format field picks a binary xlsx or a JSON payload.
In JSON mode the run-parameter sheet and both reservoirs' information sheets are read back as tables, and the upper and lower reservoir names are pulled out so the inputs can be checked.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: The workbook is split into per-reservoir inputs. Both reservoirs are then simulated together over each step: storage from the level–storage curve, losses, flood-limit storage by season, supply to users and shortfalls, top-up from the upper reservoir, and power output from head and discharge.
Each reservoir's per-step results are added up into monthly, calendar-year and hydrological-year tables plus a summary sheet. Daily tables are limited to 500 rows in the JSON.
End-of-period water level for both reservoirs, upper-reservoir inflow against generation-plus-spill outflow, and power per reservoir and in total are keyed by date and thinned to about 600 points.
The results workbook comes back with sheets for each reservoir, with the reservoir names URL-encoded in response headers. In JSON mode the same workbook is included as base64.

distinctive: Two reservoirs are run together in series: the upper one tops up downstream users from storage between set characteristic levels, and named users are cut off when the upper reservoir's storage falls too low.
Flood-limit storage changes by season (plum-rain and typhoon flood seasons). It is expanded into a day-of-year lookup with separate values for leap years.
The time step can be daily, ten-day (periods starting on the 1st, 11th and 21st) or monthly, with conversions between scales.
Results are summed by hydrological year as well as by calendar year and month, and the number of shortage periods is counted.
